h1: Nordic House & Coffee Nong Bua Lamphu — Garden Bungalows with a Café Right on Site
intro: If you want a stay in Nong Bua Lamphu that's genuinely quiet — where you can wake up, wander a flower garden and walk down to order a hot coffee without driving anywhere — Nordic House & Coffee is a place many travellers think of · It's a small boutique cluster of about 5 garden bungalows in Tambon Pho Chai, Mueang district (Road 3037), set right beside its own café and restaurant · What reviews agree on is the shady, peaceful atmosphere, a pretty flower garden, friendly service, parking at your door, and easygoing prices · From approx. ฿790/night · Real guest reviews say it suits people who want to relax and like having a café on site, rather than those who need to stay right in the centre within walking distance of everything.

body.html: Nordic House & Coffee is a small cluster of about 5 bungalow rooms at 46 Moo 1, Tambon Pho Chai, Mueang Nong Bua Lamphu, on Road 3037 · What sets it apart from the in-town hotels is that the rooms are standalone bungalows spread through a flower garden, with a café and restaurant inside the same grounds · It's a small, hands-on family-run place, suited to travellers who want privacy and a garden setting more than a long list of facilities.

There are two main room types — single-bed and double-bed rooms · Every room comes with air-con, TV, a fridge, a work desk, drinking water and a private en-suite bathroom, furnished simply in a warm, homey style · Guests like that you step out of the room straight into the garden, and can park right at your door without dragging bags far · It's exactly the kind of room upcountry travellers look for — easy to sleep in, quiet and inexpensive, without expecting anything fancy.
"Lovely shady setting with a flower garden to stroll around, really peaceful and great for resting · You can wake up and just walk down to the café out front for coffee, and the staff are sweet."

The real star here is the on-site café and restaurant, open daily (roughly 9 AM to evening) · The café side scores around 3.8/5 on Wongnai — guests praise the rich, smooth coffee at friendly prices (a hot coffee is about ฿45), with single-plate Thai dishes like pork rice soup and basil pork over rice to order too · There's both shaded outdoor seating under the trees and an air-conditioned area, with easy parking out front · For guests, having a café on site is a genuine plus — your morning coffee or first meal is steps away, no driving needed.

On location, it sits in Tambon Pho Chai towards the edge of town — about 5.5 km from the town centre and the King Naresuan the Great monument · Guests like how quiet and shady it is, but it does mean a short drive into town if you want a wider choice of dinner or to browse the night market · The upside is parking right at your door, very handy if you arrive by car or are breaking up an Isan road trip · There are restaurants and convenience stores around, though it's not as lively as the centre.

On service, it's a small place run in a friendly, hands-on way, with someone to handle check-in and help out · Most reviews speak well of the staff and the nicely kept flower garden · It wins over people who want a relaxed, garden atmosphere rather than big-hotel service.

To be honest, per real guest reviews: the main thing to know is that there are only about 5 rooms, so it fills up fast over long weekends or when there's an event in the province — book ahead · And because it's a garden stay towards the edge of town, anyone who wants a central base within walking distance of shops should plan for the drive · Facilities are small-stay level — no pool or gym — the trade-off for the budget price and a garden setting you won't find in a tower hotel.

In short, if you want a quiet stay in Nong Bua Lamphu with a flower garden to wander and good coffee on site, in the few-hundred-baht range — Nordic House & Coffee is a sensible pick · An average around 8.0 across real guest reviews reflects this well: strong on atmosphere, the café and privacy, with small caveats around the edge-of-town location and the limited number of rooms · A tip from following reviews here: if you drive, ask for a room with parking beside it, and if you're there for the café, check the opening hours first (Monday closes earlier than other days) so you can plan your morning coffee and breakfast.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Nordic House & Coffee Nong Bua Lamphu

faq.q: Where is Nordic House & Coffee in Nong Bua Lamphu, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 46 Moo 1, Tambon Pho Chai, Mueang Nong Bua Lamphu, on Road 3037 · It sits towards the edge of town, about 5.5 km from the town centre and the King Naresuan monument (around a 12-minute drive) · Close to Nong Bua Public Park and Tao To Waterfall Forest Park · The setting is quiet and shady.

faq.q: How much does Nordic House & Coffee cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿790/night for a single-bed room · Double, garden-view and family rooms run around ฿890–฿1,390 · Every room has air-con, TV, a fridge, a work desk and free Wi-Fi · Prices depend on room type and season — compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is there a café and breakfast on site?
faq.a: Yes — there's a café and restaurant right on the grounds, open daily roughly 9 AM–8 PM (earlier close on Mondays) · It serves coffee, drinks and single-plate Thai dishes like pork rice soup and basil pork over rice at friendly prices · The café scores around 3.8/5 on Wongnai, with guests praising the rich, smooth coffee.

faq.q: Who is Nordic House & Coffee best for?
faq.a: It's best for anyone who wants a quiet stay with a garden setting and a café on site, and arrives by car, in the few-hundred-baht range · Good for couples, small families or people breaking up an Isan road trip · Less suited to those who want a central base within walking distance of the market, or a pool and big-hotel service.

faq.q: Does it have parking and Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Yes — free parking right at the door and free Wi-Fi in every room · Because the rooms are standalone garden bungalows, you can park right beside your room, very handy if you drive · Every room also has a fridge and TV.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: Because there are only about 5 rooms, it fills up fast over long weekends or during provincial events, so book at least 2–3 weeks ahead · In quieter periods a week is usually enough · Choose a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't fixed.
